extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in natural language processing, scientometrics, and editors/chairs interested in automated decision prediction from peer reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Developing and evaluating models that use aspect-level information and sentiment in peer review texts to predict editorial decisions (accept/reject) and assist editors/chairs. Involves tasks such as aspect-category extraction, sentiment detection, and joint/multitask learning for decision prediction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review aspects (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviews’ opinions and sentiments about various aspects of the paper (e.g., novelty, substance, soundness, etc.) relevant to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These aspect categories (novelty, substance, soundness, etc.) are the elemental dimensions in review text that models should identify; the paper explicitly uses these aspects as inputs/features for downstream decision prediction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspect-level sentiment detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect the sentiment expressed by reviewers for each identified aspect (positive/negative/neutral) as a separate modeling task.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sentiments corresponding to aspects are treated as signals that can inform manuscript outcome prediction; the work frames sentiment detection as a task jointly learned with aspect extraction and decision prediction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspect-category extraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatically extract or classify spans/sentences in review text into aspect categories (e.g., novelty, substance, soundness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aspect-category extraction is one of the task-specific objectives in the multitask setup; accurate aspect extraction is necessary for reliable aspect-level sentiment and decision prediction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint multitask learning (aspect + sentiment + decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage aspects and their corresponding sentiments in a joint/multitask system that assists editors and chairpersons in determining manuscript outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper proposes a multitask architecture that shares representations across aspect extraction, sentiment detection, and decision prediction tasks—arguing that shared learning improves overall performance for assisting editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision prediction (acceptance/rejection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Predict the final manuscript outcome (accept or reject) from reviewer feedback and aspect-sentiment signals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The primary downstream evaluation is manuscript acceptance vs. rejection prediction; the paper reports model performance (up to 81% accuracy) on this binary decision task.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metric: accuracy for accept/reject prediction
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure model performance on the decision prediction task using accuracy (percentage of correct accept/reject predictions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper cites an achieved accuracy value (up to 81%) as an indicator of model effectiveness; accuracy is thus treated as a key quantitative evaluation metric for the decision task.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training objective: unweighted summation of task-specific losses
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine the losses from the multiple tasks (aspect extraction, sentiment detection, decision prediction) by summing them without weighting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors state they 'employ unweighted summation of the three task-specific losses' when training the multitask model; this is a specific modeling/training design choice that affects optimization and trade-offs among tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data requirement: use of Aspect-enhanced Peer Review (ASAP) Review dataset
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct experiments and evaluation on publicly available, aspect-annotated peer review datasets such as the Aspect-enhanced Peer Review (ASAP) Review dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper explicitly conducts experiments on the ASAP Review dataset; using standardized, annotated datasets is implied as necessary for reproducible benchmarking of aspect-sentiment and decision prediction systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility and code release
rubrics_metrics.description: Make code and resources public to enable future research and reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors state 'We make our code public for future research' and provide a GitHub link; releasing code and materials is treated as a best practice for reproducibility and community progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical deployment principle: assist, not replace human judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Automated systems should assist editors/chairs and not replace human judgment; promote fairness, transparency, and efficiency in editorial decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the ethics declarations the authors emphasize the aim to 'assist, not replace, human judgment' and to promote 'fairness, transparency, and efficiency'—these are normative constraints on how decision-prediction systems should be applied in practice.
